title: Covert Malicious Fine-Tune Detector via Behavioral Fingerprints

original_idea.body: # Covert Malicious Fine-Tune Detector via Behavioral Fingerprints. Build a behavioral fingerprint battery separating clean from tampered open-weight checkpoints; measure which probes best discriminate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Black-box screening for tampered open-weight checkpoints targets an AISI-flagged critical control problem.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Behavioral probe battery comparing clean vs tampered checkpoints; guided, single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused fingerprint battery + separation analysis; assembling probes is moderate effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Defends the open ecosystem, no internal access; neglected long-horizon control problem.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-based probing on public checkpoints, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Covert-finetune detection is an open problem; a behavioral-fingerprint prototype plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Open problem with some prior work; behavioral-fingerprint prototype plausibly open.
